title: Onramp Allocation Queueboard — GPU Requests (Q4 2025)
content:
Purpose:
This working tracker captures incoming GPU allocation requests (onramp/new projects + expansion requests) and moves them through a lightweight approvals pipeline. Primary audience: infra program managers, SREs, and ENG team leads who request capacity.

Context / goals:
- Reduce ad-hoc Slack asks by providing a single canonical queue
- Triage by impact + latency sensitivity so we prioritize user-facing production workloads over experimental/benchmarks
- Make approval steps explicit (cost, security, SRE) and track times-to-approve for SLAs

How to use this sheet (short):
1) Requester fills an intake row and tags their ENG lead + a minimal rollout plan (2-3 lines).
2) Infra PM (owner) does initial triage w/in 48h; assigns "Priority Score" and routes to approvers.
3) Approvals recorded inline; once green, schedule into weekly allocation batch or reserve dedicated pool.

Intake fields (columns we use):
- Request ID (RID): internal short id e.g., ONR-2025-034
- Team: team name / slack handle
- Project: short project name
- GPUs requested: count + type (eg 8x A100-80GB or 16x H100 80GB)
- Start window: earliest date they need capacity
- Duration: estimated weeks / months
- Region: primary region preference (us-west1 / eu-west1 / ap-south1)
- Workload type: training / inference / eval / devbench
- Latency sensitivity: high | medium | low
- Data sensitivity: public | internal | confidential (requires private deployment)
- Priority score: numeric (see rubric below)
- Cost lead sign-off: name + date OR Jira/Linear approval id
- Security sign-off: name + date if data sensitivity != public
- SRE feasibility: scheduled | needs config | blocked (reason)
- Status: submitted | triage | pending-approvals | approved | scheduled | denied
- Notes: free text for follow-ups, links to PRs, confluence, etc.

Priority scoring rubric (quick):
- Impact (0-5): internal metric of customer or product impact (5 = production-facing revenue traffic)
- Latency sensitivity multiplier: high=1.2, medium=1.0, low=0.8
- Duration penalty: >12 weeks => -1
Compute priority score = round((Impact * multiplier) - duration_penalty, 1)
Use score to order weekly allocation batch; tie-breaker = earliest start window.

Current queue (sample rows) — these are working examples, not final approvals:
RID | Team | Project | GPUs | Start | Dur | Region | Type | Latency | Data | Score | Cost | Security | SRE | Status | Notes
ONR-2025-028 | recommender | recx-latency-fix | 4x A100-80GB | 2025-11-10 | 6w | us-west1 | inference | high | internal | 5.8 | Priya 2025-11-04 (LIN-1123) | n/a | scheduled 2025-11-11 | requires model sharding, using local cache (See PR #198)
ONR-2025-031 | search | rerank-embedding-trials | 8x V100 | 2025-11-18 | 4w | eu-west1 | eval | low | public | 2.4 | Evan 2025-11-05 | n/a | pending-queue | pending cost review (billing diff)
ONR-2025-033 | ops | loadtesting-2025q4 | 16x H100 | 2025-12-01 | 2w | us-west1 | devbench | low | public | 1.6 | Diego 2025-11-10 | n/a | approved | ephemeral batch — schedule into 2025-12-01 weekend window
ONR-2025-035 | health-ai | privacy-eval | 12x A100-40GB | 2025-11-20 | 12w | eu-west1 | training | medium | confidential | 3.4 | Priya pending | Security requested DLP doc | needs-private | pending-security

Approval notes / flow examples:
- Cost approval: Cost lead (team-finance) must confirm estimated token-hours / run-hours fit within current committed spend. Quick approval acceptable for short (<4w) dev jobs.
- Security review: For 'confidential' data, requestor should attach a short DLP statement and select Private deployment option. Security review target 5 business days.
- SRE feasibility: SRE marks whether any infra config (nfs mounts, tuning, KV cache warmers) are needed before allocation. If 'blocked', list config items and estimated time.

Weekly cadence and owners:
- Mondays: infra PM (Marina) runs triage, updates statuses, and publishes "allocation snapshot" to #infra-allocations on Slack.
- Wednesdays: SRE scheduling call — finalize batch for Friday allocations.
- Ad-hoc: Critical P0 requests escalate to on-call SRE (page via PagerDuty).

Backlog / future considerations (notes to self):
- Add automated Linear ticket creation when a row is created (webhook) — reduces manual tracking. INFRA-402 exploration ongoing.
- Add the following computed columns in the canonical sheet: estimated run cost (USD), carbon estimate (if requested), expected tokens/hour for inference.
- Consider a dedicated 'short-lived' pool for experiments to reduce churn on large GPU reservations.

Open items (owner: Marina):
- [ ] Finalize security checklist template for confidential workloads (due: 2025-11-20).
- [x] Align on priority rubric with SRE (completed 2025-11-04).
- [ ] Run pilot for automated Linear linkage (owners: Evan + Diego).

Quick links:
- Confluence allocation runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Allocation+Runbook
- Linear board filter: https://linear.app/redwood/board/infra-capacity
- Slack channel: #infra-allocations
- Example PR for scheduling automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/287

Notes to self (informal):
- Watch eu-west1 quota — we've had soft limits on H100 there, if another training request comes in for >20 cards flag early.
- If a request is "data: confidential" and region is cloud-managed, push Private deployment conversation earlier (customer may need on-prem/no-cloud option).

End of doc — this is intentionally a working tracker. Leave comments inline when triaging and link to Linear tickets for any follow-ups.
